surfaces.part: green sign board with white text

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 14px wide from row 1 to row 30, with a 12px row 0 that acts only as the outline. It is a flat vertical signboard seen face-on. Rows 1-5 are a white header panel, a vertical face. Row 5 is a slightly darker 1-row lower edge of that panel, and no eave shadow follows it. Rows 7-27 are the green face with white lettering, and rows 28-30 are a dark base strip. There is no ellipse, roof or canopy plane, no visible contents, and no band ending in a front-edge line with shadow, so no horizontal top surface is drawn. This matches the front-elevation reference examples.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical green sign panel with a light border, light glyph marks and a dark frame. It has about 4 clear lightness steps on the panel and frame. The bus-shelter reference has only 6 visible tones per tile, and the kiosk and vending references have more. The candidate's 9 visible tones per tile sit between the bus shelter (6) and the kiosk (12), and well below the vending machine (20). Its near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for the bus shelter, so there are no large flat fills; the glyphs and border break up the panel. The dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, matching all three references, so the outline reads as a tinted dark green tone rather than a black sticker line. It is a thin, sparse object. By eye it is a little simpler than the kiosk and vending references but as rich as the accepted bus shelter, so an artist would accept it beside them.
